presentation_revision_history.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Square mature painterly mythology encyclopedia artwork of AMATERASU selecting the historically discussed ISE SNAKE-DEITY INTERPRETATION, not her usual human goddess depiction. Matsumae Takeshi, Origin and Growth of the Worship of Amaterasu (Asian Folklore Studies37.1, 1978 p5) discusses Ise traditions quoted from the medieval monk Tsūkai's Sankeiki and notes Amaterasu was regarded as a snake deity or a sun deity. Render ONE wholly natural serpent with ONE snake head, two normal serpent eyes, closed mouth, ONE continuous limbless scaled body resting in a clearly readable broad open S curve on mossy stones, ONE slender tapering tail, all comfortably inside frame. Soft bronze-gold and warm cream scale colouring chosen artistically, realistic scale texture, intelligent calm watchfulness. No hood, rattles, horn, mane, dragon limbs, wings, additional heads, human face/body or hybrid features. Sunrise rays in a tranquil ancient Japanese cedar grove near the Isuzu river, quiet distant wooden shrine roof soft in forest-green haze, radiant solar gold light around the serpent conveying sacred solar presence without bodily flame. This is an atmospheric rendering of the snake-deity scholarly interpretation: source does not identify species, colour or exact size. Do not depict sexual/bedroom story or priestess. No wolf, fox, human, mirror used as creature body, crown, clothing, talismans, weapons, copied shrine artifacts, text, border, signature or watermark. Full single snake head-to-tail coherent silhouette and reverent solar guardian mood.
